WoW: Forever

Rogue

Energy regenerates continuously, poisons and bleeds can crit, and Mutilate locks out Adrenaline Rush by exactly one talent point.

  1. Home
  2. WoW: Forever
  3. Rogue

Blizzard has published almost nothing about Rogue

The entire Rogue section of the beta development notes is one line: "Sap now correctly flags the Rogue for PvP when used on a target that is PvP flagged." Everything below is datamining and community work. A trap first. Searching for Forever Rogue hotfixes surfaces real Blizzard pages mentioning Eviscerate and other Rogue abilities. Those pages cover retail Midnight, Mists of Pandaria Classic, Season of Discovery, Burning Crusade Classic, Classic Era and Hardcore — there is no WoW Forever section on them at all. Retail Rogue tuning is not Forever Rogue tuning.

The headline changes

All four weapon specializations were deleted and folded into one talent, Hack and Slash.

WeaponAt 5 ranks
Axe or sword5% chance of an extra attack
Dagger or fist+5% critical strike chance
Maceattacks ignore 15% of target armor

This is structurally identical to Warrior's Weaponmaster. Two consequences: the mace branch deletes Classic's mace stun proc, and one-handed axes are now usable by Rogues, which is why the axe branch exists and why Orc's axe racial suddenly matters. Weapon Expertise keeps its name and does something completely different. It now reduces the chance your attacks are dodged or parried by up to 2%. Vanilla's version granted weapon skill; Forever's grants none at all. And a warning worth keeping: a miss and a dodge are different results, so the second point is not another point of hit. Energy regeneration is continuous, not ticked — smoothed to roughly 1 energy per 0.1 seconds instead of 20-energy chunks every 2 seconds. The rotational consequence is specific: Backstab and Ambush are harder to chain, because you can no longer bank a tick to land exactly when you need it. Note "continuous" is not "fast", and no source publishes an energy-per-second figure. Combo points persist per target, but the popular framing overstates it. They "persist on a target even if you swap to another, but you cannot transfer your combo points from an existing target to a new one." Per-target retention, not a pooled resource — which is exactly what the community is angry about, since points are still lost on tab-target and wasted entirely when the mob dies.

The 16-point milestone

TreeThe new 16-point talent
AssassinationCold Blood, moved down
CombatFlawless Execution — brand new, Eviscerate costs 10 less energy
SubtletyPremeditation, moved down

Worth knowing how this was resolved, because it is a lesson about datamining: one sweep concluded Forever has no 16-point milestone, because no talent carries a required-points value of 16. That is a false negative — 15 points required means available at your 16th point.

Talents

Assassination. Lethality was nerfed from 30% to 20% crit damage but widened to cover five more abilities. Improved Expose Armor was completely rewritten — from stronger armor reduction to a cheaper cost plus a 1–2 combo point refund at 5 points. Improved Kidney Shot was narrowed: Classic boosted damage from all sources, Forever only from your own attacks and poisons. Murder lost Beasts and Dragonkin. Improved Poisons gained a 10–50% chance not to consume a charge. Vigor raises maximum energy, not regeneration. Seal Fate now reaches 100%. Combat took two real nerfs. Precision was gutted from 5 ranks at 5% hit to 3 ranks at 3% — a straight −2% hit for every Combat rogue. Dual Wield Specialization was halved, from 5×10% to 5×5% off-hand damage. Against that, Improved Eviscerate was buffed and Puncturing Wounds moved here from Assassination, giving Backstab a 45% chance of a bonus combo point. Subtlety got the most new material. Quietus adds damage below 35% health, Cutthroat gives Backstab a chance that your next Ambush needs no Stealth, and the capstone Thousand Cuts cuts your next Hemorrhage or Backstab cost as Rupture ticks. Setup and Initiative both reach 100%, large buffs. Dirty Deeds means Garrote no longer requires being behind the target. Hemorrhage's rework is the headline and it is a loss. Classic Hemorrhage added damage to the raid's physical attacks. Forever's supports your bleed instead — +15% Rupture damage from you. Subtlety no longer brings a group physical-damage debuff. Removed from Subtlety: Sleight of Hand, Deadliness, and Improved Sap — the last because Sap no longer breaks Stealth in Forever, so the talent had nothing to do.

The two new abilities

Mutilate — Assassination 21-point, 60 energy, instant, daggers only. Both weapons for 75% weapon damage plus a flat bonus each, +20% against poisoned targets, awards 2 combo points. It does not consume poison stacks and does not require attacking from behind, and because it uses both weapons directly, off-hand weapon damage matters for the builder itself. A live tuning tell: the flat bonus was +13 in a 17 September snapshot and +17 at the current build. Venom — the capstone, requires Mutilate. Increases your poison damage by 30% and application chance by 10%. Combo points buy duration only, not a larger bonus. It is a self-buff, not a damaging finisher, and it is not eligible for Cold Blood. It is not Envenom.

Poisons

Poison damage now scales with Attack Power, and poisons and bleeds can crit — a genuine departure from 1.12. That makes crit matter to Rupture, Garrote and every poison tick. Poisons still have charges, now alongside a one-hour duration, and charges run out first in practice. They stack with Sharpening Stones and with Windfury Totem — which has the rare distinction of being Blizzard-confirmed: "Windfury and weapon enhancements/poisons stacked on the Blizzcon demo which was level 38." One subtlety that will cost you damage: a coating is not a target debuff. Instant Poison's immediate damage does not by itself leave a poison effect; Deadly Poison does. Mutilate's +20% needs an actual poison sitting on the enemy. Poison base damage was cut across all ranks, with one tester estimating roughly 30% and no compensation.

Rotation

At 20, Combat and Assassination share an identical priority, which tells you the specs have not diverged: Instant Poison on both weapons, Stealth into Ambush, Backstab from behind or Sinister Strike otherwise, then Slice and Dice at 5 points if the target lives its full duration, else Eviscerate. It is described plainly as "two buttons" plus utility, and Combat is the safest levelling route. Subtlety is the weakest at 20 and Rupture is usually not worth casting — "even on targets that live the full duration, you're better off using Slice and Dice." The Gouge into Backstab setup is the only non-Stealth way behind a target early: wait until you are near max energy before Gouging, or the window closes before you can afford Backstab. Weapon-swap macros are genuinely part of level-20 play — dagger for Ambush, slow main hand for Sinister Strike. Swapping costs a GCD and resets your swing timer, and the macros need pressing twice.

The forced shape at 60

Venom needs 31 Assassination and requires Mutilate. Adrenaline Rush needs 31 Combat. Thousand Cuts needs 31 Subtlety.

Mutilate and Adrenaline Rush cannot coexist. Mutilate needs at least 21 Assassination and Adrenaline Rush needs 31 Combat — a 52-point minimum against a 51-point budget. The same exclusion kills Mutilate plus Thousand Cuts.

Forever forbids the dagger-Mutilate/Adrenaline-Rush hybrid by exactly one point. What the spare points buy: Cold Blood at 16 Assassination fits alongside Adrenaline Rush, and Flawless Execution at 16 Combat fits alongside Venom — though it is worth less to a build spending most finishers on poison upkeep.

Stats

Weapon damage is king, then hit and Expertise, then Agility, then crit. Subtlety's guide is the weapon-speed-aware one: favour slow main hands — "between a 15 DPS weapon that has a 1.9 speed, and a 14 DPS weapon with a 2.8 speed, the 2.8 speed one will serve you better." Does 1.12 hit-cap theory still hold? Partly, and nobody has published the numbers. A yellow and white distinction appears to survive — "shared stats still do not mean every attack has an identical hit requirement" is the two-roll model still speaking — but that is an inference from careful phrasing, not a stated cap split. No hit cap number exists anywhere for Rogue. On the dual-wield miss penalty there is no evidence of change and no confirmation of retention; one player asserts 19%, in a thread reporting a 70–80% miss rate with dual daggers at level 10. Two poison-gearing traps both careful guides shut down: unified hit and crit does not mean poisons scale with spell power, and armor penetration and the Hack and Slash mace branch do nothing for poison damage or bleeds.

Race

Tauren remains the only Classic race that cannot be a Rogue. Skyborne can, on either faction. Human Sword Specialization is +2%, double every other weapon racial. Orc Axe Specialization is newly relevant, because Rogues can use one-handed axes now. Dwarf gained Mace Specialization, new to the race. Night Elf's Elune's Light — +10% crit for 15 seconds — is arguably the strongest new Rogue racial in the game, because it is an on-use burst window that pairs with Adrenaline Rush. Dwarf Stoneform now gives flat 10% physical damage reduction plus bleed, poison and disease immunity.

Sentiment

Negative and specific. Combat levelling is considered weak, with an itemised case: Eviscerate feeling weak despite 3/3 Improved Eviscerate, Precision's cut hurting early hit, Dual Wield Spec's halving reducing white damage, poison damage down with no compensation. Both new capstones are disliked — "terrible designs and completely useless in pvp" — and Thousand Cuts drew "100% the wrong direction". Combo points are the loudest complaint. Dual-wielding at level 10 is reported as a DPS loss versus a single weapon. Counterpoint, from a tester who finds the class smooth: they prefer spending finishers at 2–3 combo points, because "building all the way to 5 combo points often feels too expensive in terms of energy and time." No Blizzard reply appears in any Rogue feedback thread.

Still unknown

Any hit cap value, and whether the yellow and white split survives. Whether the dual-wield miss penalty changed. Energy regeneration in numbers, base pool, and the GCD. Cloak of Shadows, mentioned by no source. Redirect, datamined but not on any trainer. And Restless Blades, which one guide's prose describes as a Combat talent — it appears nowhere in that same site's own talent data. Almost certainly stale pre-beta text.
